html:
A Zulu church founded in 1910 by the prophet and healer Isaiah Shembe in Natal, South Africa. Its members are called amaNazaretha. It is one of the largest African-initiated churches, founded and led by Africans rather than by foreign missions.

Shembe drew on the Bible, especially the Old Testament, and on Zulu custom. Members keep Saturday as the Sabbath, worship barefoot, and wear distinctive dress. Sacred dance and hymns, many written by Shembe himself, are at the heart of worship. The church built its holy village, Ekuphakameni, near Durban, and holds yearly pilgrimages to the mountain of Nhlangakazi.

At a time when Africans were losing land and rights, the church offered a community under African leadership. After Isaiah Shembe died in 1935, his sons led it; later disputes split it into rival branches. It is often compared with other African churches such as that of Simon Kimbangu in the Congo and the Celestial Church of Christ in West Africa.
